items.title: Voters deliver "AI earthquake," rebuking tech and billionaires
items.summary:
AI had its "official debut" as the biggest issue in American politics, former New York Assemblymember and RAISE Act author Alex Bores told Axios. "AI is reaching into every part of our society and economy and it's now crystal clear it's impacting every part of our politics, too." [...] Voters showed deep distrust of the AI race Tuesday, approving dozens of data center moratoriums and electing a raft of candidates who favor slowing a $10 trillion buildout, including in Texas — the epicenter of the boom.

Why it matters: In an election that hinged on an affordability crisis for many Americans, voters made it clear they view Silicon Valley's AI ambitions not as a technological miracle, but as a resource-draining threat to their wallets and communities. [...] Democratic challengers successfully weaponized AI policy, ousting Republicans in Ohio, Wisconsin, Arizona and Pennsylvania.

items.title: A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.
items.summary:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

Accelerating biological research starts with getting the everyday work right. BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

items.title: AI agent testing reveals a risky future of 'teamwork' inside companies
items.summary:
AI agents have been caught circumventing restrictions, communicating through unauthorized channels and pursuing goals in ways their creators did not intend. The most high-profile example emerged last summer when OpenAI disclosed that its models found ways to communicate through improvised channels, bypass internet restrictions and hack into an outside system, Hugging Face. [...] In research published by Anthropic and collaborators, researchers describe multi-agent systems as "AI organizations" — groups of agents with different roles that communicate and work toward a common goal. The researchers tested these organizations in simulated business-consulting and software-development settings, and specifically, to assess whether when the agents work as a team they will break rules to reach specified goals. [...] Groups of AI agents often performed worse than their strongest member, even when they knew which agent was the expert. Rather than taking advantage of the expert's knowledge, agents tended to compromise between expert and non-expert opinions. The researchers found that this tendency toward compromise increased with team size and was associated with poorer performance.

"Collective failures don't necessarily require individual agents to behave badly," Cao, one of the study's authors, said.

items.title: CrowdStrike Introduces AI Kill Switch
items.summary:
Coming soon, CrowdStrike will extend AI Kill Switch beyond gateway enforcement to deliver coordinated agent containment across the Falcon platform.

AI agents operate across endpoints, cloud environments, SaaS applications, browsers, and enterprise identities, often spanning multiple environments in a single chain of activity. When an agent goes rogue, stopping it shouldn't require security teams to investigate and respond separately in every environment. [...] Rather than responding to isolated events through disconnected tools, security teams will be able to coordinate containment across the agentic attack surface.

## Secure AI Adoption Without Losing Control

AI agents are becoming a powerful part of enterprise operations. As their autonomy and reach expand, organizations need security that can keep pace.

items.title: Exclusive: Meet "sovereign agents," AI that keeps itself alive
items.summary:
Photo illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Photo: Carsten Koall/Getty Images

AI agents that pursue their own open-ended survival are an emerging security threat, according to a report first shared with Axios from the Center for a New American Security. [...] The length of tasks AI agents can finish on their own has doubled roughly every three and a half months since 2024, according to testing by the AI evaluator METR.
   And they're turning to hacking even when no one asks. In the past month alone, it's been revealed that an Anthropic model filed visa applications and sent Philadelphia police a made-up homicide tip, and banks caught agents acting in customer accounts seemingly on their own. [...] Expel CTO Greg Notch called the idea of a malicious AI swarm "far-fetched."
   Unlike traditional botnets, AI agents need costly computing power, which gives defenders "a clear leash we've never had on a botnet," SANS Institute's Rob T. Lee told Axios.

What's next: Existing safeguards "may still offer partial protection," the report says, since frontier AI companies already train their models to refuse hacking.
